topics.title: Financial Needs and Classification of Financial Sources
explain: Business financial requirements are grouped by duration into long-term, medium-term, and short-term needs.
Long-term financial needs exceed 5 to 10 years and fund fixed assets like plant, machinery, land, and permanent working capital.
Medium-term financial needs range between 1 and 5 years, required for stores, spares, tools, dies, and moulds.
Short-term financial needs are up to 1 year, required to finance current assets like stock, debtors, and cash.
Financial sources can be classified by basic source (internal vs external), maturity of payment, or ownership (owner's funds vs borrowed funds).

flow.title: Matching Financial Needs to Funding Sources
steps: Identify asset requirement duration
Select short term for working capital
Select medium term for spares and tools
Select long term for fixed assets

topics.example: Purchasing land for a new factory requires long-term equity or debenture funds, while buying raw material inventory uses short-term trade credit.
remember: Long-term needs exceed 5-10 years.
Medium-term needs cover 1-5 years.
Short-term needs are up to 1 year.
mistakes: Using short-term borrowings to fund long-term fixed assets causes severe liquidity and repayment mismatches.

quiz.q: What is the duration specified for medium-term financial needs?
o: Exceeding 1 year but not exceeding 5 years
quiz.why: Medium-term needs refer to funds required for a period exceeding 1 year but not exceeding 5 years.

quiz.q: Funds required to finance permanent or hard-core working capital should be procured from:
quiz.why: Hard-core permanent working capital is constantly needed by the business and must be funded from long-term sources.

topics.title: Equity Share Capital and Retained Earnings
explain: Equity share capital is permanent capital provided by owners who undertake the highest risk in the company.
Equity dividends are paid after meeting all other claims and represent an appropriation of profits, not a tax-deductible charge.
Issuing equity increases the financial base and debt-raising capacity, but may dilute earnings per share (EPS) and control.
Retained earnings involve ploughing back company profits into the business to finance expansion.
Retained earnings entail no flotation costs, cause no control dilution, and carry minimal financial risk.

flow.title: Allocation of Net Profit to Retained Earnings
steps: Generate operational net profit
Pay obligatory interest and taxes
Pay preference share dividends
Retain portion of residual profit
Reinvest retained earnings into business

topics.example: A company generates ₹100 lakh net profit, pays ₹30 lakh as dividend, and retains ₹70 lakh in reserves to fund a new warehouse without issuing fresh shares.
remember: Equity dividend is an appropriation of profit, not a tax-deductible expense.
Equity shares provide permanent capital with no redemption liability.
mistakes: Believing equity capital is cost-free; equity actually has the highest cost of capital due to maximum risk expected by equity investors.

quiz.q: Dividends payable to equity shareholders are treated as:
quiz.why: Equity dividend is paid after all claims are satisfied and represents an appropriation of profit.

quiz.q: Which long-term internal source of finance avoids flotation costs and dilution of control?
quiz.why: Retained earnings use internal accumulated profits, incurring no flotation expenses or control dilution.

topics.title: Preference Share Capital
explain: Preference shares carry priority over equity shares for fixed dividend payment and capital repayment upon winding up.
Preference capital is a hybrid instrument combining equity features (dividend is non-deductible) and debt features (fixed dividend rate).
Cumulative preference shares accumulate unpaid dividend arrears during loss years to be paid out in future profitable years.
Preference shares generally do not dilute voting control of equity holders because preference shareholders have limited voting rights.
Preference dividends are not tax-deductible, making preference capital costlier to the firm than debt.

flow.title: Classification of Preference Shares
steps: Cumulative accumulates unpaid dividend arrears
Non-cumulative forfeits unpaid past dividends
Participating shares extra surplus profits
Convertible converts into equity shares
Redeemable repays capital on maturity

topics.example: If a company skips paying a 10% dividend on cumulative preference shares in Year 1 due to losses, it must pay 20% in Year 2 before equity shareholders receive any dividend.
remember: Preference dividend is not tax-deductible.
Cumulative preference share dividend arrears accumulate until paid.
mistakes: Assuming preference shareholders have voting rights identical to equity shareholders on all company decisions.

quiz.q: Preference share capital is described as a hybrid financing instrument because:
o: It is issued jointly by banks and government
It combines equity characteristics with fixed debt returns
It can be used for both short and long term
It carries full voting rights and tax benefits
quiz.why: It resembles equity because dividends are non-deductible appropriations and resembles debt due to a fixed dividend rate.

quiz.q: What happens to unpaid dividends on cumulative preference shares in a loss-making year?
o: They convert automatically into equity shares
They accumulate and carry forward to future years
They are paid immediately by the government
quiz.why: Cumulative preference share dividends accumulate over loss years and must be paid when profits become available.

topics.title: Debentures and Bonds
explain: Debentures are long-term debt instruments issued under a debenture trust deed at fixed interest rates, typically for 3 to 10 years.
Interest on debentures is tax-deductible, reducing the effective cost of debt compared to equity and preference capital.
Public issues of debentures require mandatory credit ratings from rating agencies like CRISIL.
Callable bonds give the issuer the right to redeem early, while puttable bonds give the investor the right to sell back early.
Specialized bonds include Masala Bonds (rupee-denominated issued abroad), Plain Vanilla Bonds, and Foreign Currency Convertible Bonds (FCCBs).

flow.title: Process of Raising Funds via Debentures
steps: Draft debenture trust deed
Obtain credit rating from CRISIL
Issue debentures to public or institutions
Pay periodic tax-deductible interest
Redeem principal at maturity

topics.example: An Indian firm issues Masala Bonds in London to raise ₹2,000 crore in Indian Rupees, avoiding foreign currency exchange fluctuation risk.
remember: Debenture interest is a tax-deductible expense.
Masala bonds are rupee-denominated bonds issued in overseas markets.
mistakes: Confusing Masala Bonds with foreign currency bonds; Masala Bonds are denominated in Indian Rupees, protecting the issuer from currency risk.

quiz.q: Why is the effective cost of debenture financing lower than equity or preference shares?
o: Debenture interest is a tax-deductible expense
quiz.why: Interest paid on debentures reduces taxable income, providing a tax shield that lowers the net cost of debt.

quiz.q: A bond that gives the issuer the right to redeem it before its maturity date is a:
quiz.why: A callable bond contains a call option allowing the issuer to redeem the bond prior to maturity.

topics.title: Loans from Financial Institutions, Commercial Banks, and Bridge Finance
explain: National financial institutions like IFCI, SFCs, IDBI, ICICI, and LIC provide long and medium-term term loans for industrial expansion.
International institutions providing financial support include IBRD (World Bank), IFC, and Asian Development Bank (ADB).
Commercial banks provide long-term loans, Working Capital Term Loans (WCTL), and short-term credit facilities.
Bridge finance refers to temporary short-term loans granted by commercial banks while long-term loans sanctioned by financial institutions are pending disbursement.
Bridge loans carry higher interest rates and are secured by hypothecating movable assets or promissory notes.

flow.title: Bridge Finance Process
steps: Financial institution sanctions long term loan
Formal disbursement process faces temporary delay
Commercial bank grants short term bridge loan
Project starts without losing time
Term loan disburses and pays bridge loan

topics.example: A manufacturing firm gets a ₹50 crore term loan sanctioned by an institution, but takes a ₹5 crore bridge loan from a bank to start construction while paperwork is finalized.
remember: Bridge finance covers the gap between loan sanction and final disbursement.
IBRD (World Bank) was established in 1944.
mistakes: Treating bridge finance as a long-term loan facility; it is a short-term temporary advance.

quiz.q: Bridge finance is primarily obtained by a company to:
o: Cover the time gap until sanctioned long-term loans are disbursed
quiz.why: Bridge finance is a short-term bank loan used temporarily pending disbursement of sanctioned long-term institutional loans.

quiz.q: Which of the following international financial institutions was established in 1944?
o: International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD)
Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India (ICICI)
quiz.why: The World Bank / IBRD was established in 1944.

topics.title: Venture Capital Financing and Debt Securitisation
explain: Venture capital financing provides equity or debt funding to high-risk, high-potential new ventures promoted by qualified entrepreneurs.
Venture capitalists offer managerial expertise, sales strategy, and business networking in addition to funds.
Venture funding methods include equity financing (holding max 49%), conditional loans (repayable as sales royalty), income notes, and participating debentures.
Debt Securitisation pools illiquid financial assets (like car loans) and converts them into marketable debt securities via a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV).
Securitisation removes illiquid assets from the originator's balance sheet, generating immediate cash to fund new loans.

flow.title: Debt Securitisation Mechanism
steps: Originator grants loans to retail borrowers
Originator sells loan pool to SPV
SPV converts loan pool into securities
SPV sells securities to investors
Debtors pay SPV and investors get returns

topics.example: A finance company sells ₹100 crore of auto loans to an SPV; the SPV issues marketable securities to investors, allowing the finance company to issue new auto loans.
remember: Venture capital equity holding usually does not exceed 49% to leave control with the entrepreneur.
Securitisation converts illiquid assets into liquid marketable securities.
mistakes: Assuming debt securitisation changes the original debtor's payment terms; borrowers usually continue paying existing loan instalments as usual.

quiz.q: In venture capital financing, conditional loans are repayable in the form of:
o: Fixed monthly bank interest from day one
Royalty on sales after the venture generates revenue
quiz.why: Conditional loans charge zero initial interest and are repayable as royalty on sales once commercial operations begin.

quiz.q: The Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) in debt securitisation serves to:
o: Pool illiquid loans and issue marketable securities to investors
Audit the financial statements of originators
quiz.why: The SPV buys the pool of illiquid loans from the finance company and converts them into marketable securities.

topics.title: Lease Financing
explain: Leasing is a contract where the asset owner (lessor) grants use of an asset to the user (lessee) for periodic rental payments.
An Operating Lease is short-term, cancelable, shorter than economic life, and the lessor bears insurance, maintenance, and obsolescence risks.
A Financial Lease is long-term, non-cancelable, covers the asset's full economic life, and the lessee bears maintenance and obsolescence costs.
In a Sales and Lease Back transaction, an asset owner sells the asset to a buyer and immediately leases it back to retain physical use while raising cash.
Other lease structures include Leveraged Lease (using a 3rd party lender), Sales-aid Lease, Close-ended Lease, and Open-ended Lease.

flow.title: Financial vs Operating Lease Decision
steps: Determine required asset usage period
If short term and cancelable select Operating Lease
Lessor retains ownership and maintenance duties
If full economic life select Financial Lease
Lessee assumes maintenance and obsolescence risk

topics.example: An IT company leasing laptops for 2 years with the option to return them avoids technological obsolescence via an Operating Lease.
remember: Financial lease is non-cancelable and transfers risk of obsolescence to the lessee.
Operating lease is cancelable and shorter than the economic life of the asset.
mistakes: Believing legal title transfers to the lessee at the start of a lease; the lessor retains legal title throughout.

quiz.q: Which feature distinguishes an operating lease from a financial lease?
o: It is non-cancelable and spans full economic life
The lessee bears all maintenance and insurance expenses
It is short-term, cancelable, and lessor bears obsolescence risk
The lessee amortises the total capital outlay of the lessor
quiz.why: Operating leases are short-term, cancelable agreements where maintenance and obsolescence risks stay with the lessor.

quiz.q: What occurs during a Sales and Lease Back arrangement?
o: The asset is physically shifted to a supplier
The owner sells the asset and leases it back immediately
The lessor cancels the lease contract without notice
The asset is destroyed and claimed under insurance
quiz.why: The owner sells the asset to receive cash and leases it back from the buyer to retain uninterrupted physical use.

topics.title: Short-Term Sources of Finance and Bank Advances
explain: Trade Credit is credit extended by suppliers (15 to 90 days); it is a spontaneous, cost-free source that grows with business volume.
Accrued expenses (wages, taxes) and deferred income (advances) act as spontaneous short-term sources of finance.
Commercial Paper (CP) is an unsecured promissory note issued in minimum denominations of ₹5 lakhs or multiples thereof.
Treasury Bills (T-Bills) are short-term Central Government debt securities with maturities between 14 to 364 days.
Certificates of Deposit (CD) are bank time deposit receipts issued for 7 days up to 1 year, transferable in secondary markets.
Bank facilities include Short-Term Loans, Overdraft, Clean Overdraft, Cash Credit (against pledge/hypothecation), and Bills Discounting.

flow.title: Commercial Paper Issuance Process
steps: Highly rated corporate plans short term borrowing
Obtain credit rating from CRISIL or ICRA
Issue unsecured CPs in five lakh multiples
Link interest rate to one-year government bond yield
Redeem CP on maturity date

topics.example: A large corporation issues Commercial Paper worth ₹25 lakhs (5 units of ₹5 lakhs) at a discount to fund working capital requirements for 90 days.
remember: Commercial Paper minimum denomination is ₹5 lakhs.
T-Bill maturities range between 14 and 364 days.
Trade credit duration is typically 15 to 90 days.
mistakes: Confusing Cash Credit with Overdraft; Cash Credit is sanctioned against pledge or hypothecation of goods, whereas Overdraft is granted on a Current Account limit.

quiz.q: Commercial Papers (CP) are issued in minimum denominations of:
quiz.why: Commercial Papers are money market instruments issued in denominations of ₹5 lakhs or multiples thereof.

quiz.q: Treasury Bills (T-Bills) issued by the Government of India have maturity periods ranging between:
quiz.why: T-Bills meet short-term government borrowing requirements with maturities ranging between 14 and 364 days.

topics.title: Export Trade Financing by Banks
explain: Commercial banks provide short-term export finance in Rupees or foreign currency through Pre-shipment and Post-shipment credit.
Pre-shipment finance (Packing Credit) funds buying, manufacturing, processing, and packing goods prior to export.
Packing credit must be liquidated within 180 days from commencement using export bill proceeds.
Types of packing credit include Clean credit, credit against hypothecation, pledge, ECGC guarantee, and forward exchange contracts.
Post-shipment finance includes purchasing/discounting documentary export bills, ECGC guarantees, and advances against duty drawbacks.
Inter-Corporate Deposits (ICDs) and Public Deposits (max 35% of paid-up capital & reserves, 6 months to 3 years) are other short/medium-term sources.

flow.title: Export Financing Lifecycle
steps: Exporter receives firm order or Letter of Credit
Bank grants Pre-shipment Packing Credit
Goods manufactured packed and shipped overseas
Bank provides Post-shipment Bill Discounting
Export proceeds liquidate packing credit within 180 days

topics.example: A textile exporter uses pre-shipment packing credit to buy yarn, manufactures shirts, exports them to Europe, and repays the bank advance within 180 days.
remember: Packing credit must be liquidated within 180 days.
Public deposits cannot exceed 35% of paid-up capital and reserves.
mistakes: Believing public deposits can be used to purchase long-term fixed assets; they are meant only to finance working capital.

quiz.q: Pre-shipment packing credit granted by commercial banks must be liquidated within a maximum period of:
quiz.why: Packing credit is a short-term advance required to be liquidated within 180 days from commencement.

quiz.q: What is the maximum limit up to which a company can accept public deposits relative to its paid-up capital and reserves?
quiz.why: As per RBI stipulations, a company can accept public deposits up to a maximum of 35 per cent of its paid-up capital and reserves.

topics.title: Other Innovative Debt Instruments and Funding Sources
explain: Seed Capital Assistance (IDBI scheme) provides interest-free assistance with a 1% service charge for technically qualified entrepreneurs.
Deep Discount Bonds / Zero Coupon Bonds pay no periodic interest; they are sold at a discount and redeemed at face value upon maturity.
Inflation Bonds adjust interest rates for inflation to protect investor returns from purchasing power loss.
High Yield Bonds (Junk Bonds) are rated below investment grade, offering higher interest rates to compensate for high default risk.
Other financial instruments include Deferred Payment Guarantees, Capital Incentives, Secured Premium Notes, and Zero Interest Fully Convertible Debentures.

flow.title: Working Mechanism of Zero Coupon / Deep Discount Bond
steps: Issuer sells bond at deep discount
Investor pays discounted price upfront
No periodic interest paid during lock-in period
Issuer pays full face value upon maturity
Difference represents total interest earned

topics.example: A Deep Discount Bond with face value ₹10,000 is issued today for ₹2,500 for 15 years; the ₹7,500 difference is the investor's gain at maturity.
remember: Zero coupon / deep discount bonds make no periodic interest payments.
Junk bonds carry low credit ratings and high default risks.
mistakes: Assuming junk bonds are risk-free government securities; they carry high risk of default.

quiz.q: Bonds rated below investment grade that offer higher interest rates due to elevated default risk are called:
quiz.why: Junk bonds have low credit ratings and compensate investors for high default risk by paying higher yields.

quiz.q: The Seed Capital Assistance scheme introduced by IDBI features:
o: Interest-free loans with 1% initial service charge
quiz.why: Seed Capital Assistance is interest-free for technically qualified entrepreneurs, bearing only a 1% per annum service charge initially.

topics.title: International Financing and Financial Instruments
explain: International financing allows firms to raise funds via commercial banks, development banks, trade bill discounting, and international capital markets.
External Commercial Borrowings (ECBs) are commercial loans from non-resident lenders with a minimum average maturity of 3 years.
ECBs can be accessed via Automatic Route (no RBI/Govt approval needed) or Approval Route (RBI/Govt approval required).
American Depository Receipts (ADRs) are securities issued by non-US companies to list and trade specifically on US stock exchanges.
Global Depository Receipts (GDRs) are negotiable certificates traded in international markets (mainly Europe/London) representing underlying equity shares.
Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) bonds include Green Bonds (funding eco-friendly projects), Social Bonds, and Sustainability-Linked Bonds (SLBs).

flow.title: ADR / GDR Issuance Mechanism
steps: Domestic company deposits shares with domestic custodian
Overseas depository bank issues depository receipts
ADRs or GDRs listed on foreign stock exchanges
Foreign investors buy receipts in foreign currency
Company raises foreign capital directly

topics.example: Ghaziabad Municipal Corporation raised ₹150 crore in 2021 by issuing Green Bonds to finance an eco-friendly water supply project.
remember: Minimum average maturity for ECBs is 3 years.
ADRs trade on US stock exchanges; GDRs trade primarily on European exchanges.
mistakes: Confusing ADRs with GDRs; ADRs are exclusively listed on US stock exchanges.

quiz.q: What is the minimum average maturity period required for raising External Commercial Borrowings (ECBs)?
quiz.why: ECBs refer to commercial loans availed from non-resident lenders with a minimum average maturity of 3 years.

quiz.q: Securities offered by non-US companies seeking listing specifically on US stock exchanges are called:
quiz.why: ADRs are securities offered by non-US companies specifically to list on US stock exchanges.

topics.title: Contemporary Sources of Funding: Crowdfunding
explain: Crowdfunding involves raising money from a large group of people via online platforms (social media and dedicated websites).
The crowdfunding process involves three key parties: fund raiser, mediator (online platform), and fund investor/donor.
Equity Crowdfunding allows investors to contribute money in exchange for equity securities in early-stage startups.
Peer-to-Peer (P2P) Lending matches individual lenders directly with borrowers to provide unsecured online loans with interest returns.
Donation-based Crowdfunding collects funds for charitable, social, or medical causes without granting ownership or debt claims.

flow.title: P2P Crowdfunding Process
steps: Borrower submits loan request on P2P platform
Platform assesses creditworthiness and lists project
Multiple individual lenders pool small fund amounts
Borrower receives loan and makes monthly repayments
Platform distributes principal and interest to lenders

topics.example: A tech startup raises ₹20 lakhs by receiving ₹10,000 each from 200 retail investors via an online equity crowdfunding platform like StartEngine.
remember: P2P lending facilitates unsecured online loans directly between individuals.
Donation-based crowdfunding creates no equity or debt obligations.
mistakes: Assuming donation-based crowdfunding creates a debt repayment obligation for the fundraiser.

quiz.q: In Peer-to-Peer (P2P) lending, loans extended through online platforms are typically:
o: Unsecured loans matched directly between lenders and borrowers
quiz.why: P2P lending matches individual lenders with borrowers to provide unsecured loans through online platforms.

quiz.q: Which type of crowdfunding raises money for medical or charity causes without offering equity or debt returns?
quiz.why: Donation-based crowdfunding collects money as charity for causes with no expectation of ownership or debt repayment.
